coverage: All twenty-three scenes in both original-en and modern-en: named cast, speaking and stage roles, the named French and English nobility of the battle rolls, and the historical, classical and religious figures cited in the play.

entities.name: King Henry V
entities.body: The young King of England, who presses a claim to the crown of France.

snapshots.body: The King of England, who gives Pistol the name Harry le Roy while he walks the camp unknown.
The King of England, victor on the field the heralds name Agincourt.

entities.name: The King of France
entities.body: The French king, Katharine’s father; the play never gives his name.

entities.name: The Dauphin
entities.body: The French king’s son and heir, who sends King Henry a mocking gift.

entities.name: The Constable of France
entities.body: Charles Delabreth, High Constable of France and commander of its army.

entities.name: Fluellen
entities.body: A Welsh captain in the English army, devoted to the ancient disciplines of war.

entities.name: Pistol
entities.body: An ensign in the English army, formerly of Falstaff’s London company.

snapshots.body: An ensign in the English army, now married to the Hostess.

entities.name: The Duke of Exeter
entities.body: King Henry’s uncle, who carries his demands to the French court.

entities.name: Princess Katharine
entities.body: The French king’s daughter, whom King Henry claims as part of his terms.

snapshots.body: The French king’s daughter, named by King Henry as the first article of his terms.

entities.name: The Chorus
entities.body: The speaker who opens each act and asks the audience to imagine what the stage cannot show.

entities.name: Montjoy
entities.body: The French herald, who carries his king’s messages to King Henry.

entities.name: The Archbishop of Canterbury
entities.body: The Archbishop, who lays out King Henry’s claim to France.

entities.name: The Duke of Orleans
entities.body: Charles, Duke of Orleans, a French nobleman and the king’s nephew.

entities.name: Gower
entities.body: An English captain and Fluellen’s friend.

entities.name: Michael Williams
entities.body: A soldier in the English army who argues with the disguised King on the eve of battle.

entities.name: The Duke of Gloucester
entities.body: King Henry’s brother, who directs the siege works at Harfleur.

entities.name: The Duke of Bedford
entities.body: King Henry’s brother.

entities.name: The Duke of Clarence
entities.body: King Henry’s brother.

entities.name: The Earl of Westmorland
entities.body: An English nobleman of King Henry’s council.

entities.name: The Earl of Warwick
entities.body: An English nobleman in King Henry’s train.

entities.name: The Earl of Salisbury
entities.body: An English nobleman who takes his charge before Agincourt.

entities.name: The Earl of Huntingdon
entities.body: An English nobleman at the French court for the peace terms.

entities.name: The Duke of York
entities.body: Edward, Duke of York, who asks to lead the vanguard at Agincourt.

entities.name: The Bishop of Ely
entities.body: The Bishop, who presses King Henry’s French claim alongside Canterbury.

entities.name: Lord Scroop
entities.body: Henry, Lord Scroop of Masham, one of King Henry’s intimates.

entities.name: The Earl of Cambridge
entities.body: Richard, Earl of Cambridge.

entities.name: Sir Thomas Grey
entities.body: A knight of Northumberland.

entities.name: Sir Thomas Erpingham
entities.body: An old English knight, whose cloak the King borrows the night before Agincourt.

entities.name: Captain Jamy
entities.body: A Scottish captain in the English army.

entities.name: Captain Macmorris
entities.body: An Irish captain in the English army, in charge of the mines at Harfleur.

entities.name: John Bates
entities.body: A soldier in the English army.

entities.name: Alexander Court
entities.body: A soldier in the English army; not the Macedonian king Fluellen argues about later.

entities.name: Bardolph
entities.body: A lieutenant in the English army, formerly of Falstaff’s London company.

snapshots.body: A lieutenant of the English army, condemned for robbing a church.

entities.name: Nym
entities.body: A corporal in the English army, formerly of Falstaff’s London company.

entities.name: The Hostess
entities.body: Nell Quickly, who keeps a London tavern and has married Pistol.

snapshots.body: Nell Quickly, who keeps a London tavern and has married Pistol.

entities.name: The Boy
entities.body: The boy who serves Pistol, Bardolph and Nym, and interprets for Pistol in France.

entities.name: Queen Isabel
entities.body: The Queen of France, Katharine’s mother.

entities.name: Alice
entities.body: An old gentlewoman attending Princess Katharine, who has been in England.

entities.name: The Duke of Burgundy
entities.body: The French duke who brokers the meeting between the two kings.

entities.name: The Duke of Bourbon
entities.body: John, Duke of Bourbon, a French nobleman.

entities.name: Lord Rambures
entities.body: A French lord, master of the crossbows.

entities.name: Lord Grandpré
entities.body: A French lord who describes the English army on the morning of Agincourt.

entities.name: The Duke of Berry
entities.body: A French duke summoned to the defence.

entities.name: The Duke of Brittany
entities.body: A French duke summoned to the defence.

entities.name: The Duke of Brabant
entities.body: Anthony, Duke of Brabant, brother to the Duke of Burgundy.

entities.name: The Duke of Alençon
entities.body: John, Duke of Alençon, from whose helmet King Henry took a glove.

entities.name: The Duke of Bar
entities.body: Edward, Duke of Bar, a French nobleman.

entities.name: Jacques Chatillon
entities.body: Admiral of France.

entities.name: Lord Boucicault
entities.body: A French lord, taken prisoner at Agincourt.

entities.name: Sir Guichard Dauphin
entities.body: Great Master of France; a nobleman of that surname, not the king’s son.

entities.name: Vaudemont
entities.body: A French earl named among the dead at Agincourt.

entities.name: Beaumont
entities.body: A French earl named among the dead at Agincourt.

entities.name: Roussi
entities.body: A French earl named among the dead at Agincourt.

entities.name: Fauconbridge
entities.body: A French earl named among the dead at Agincourt.

entities.name: Foix
entities.body: A French earl named among the dead at Agincourt.

entities.name: Lestrale
entities.body: A French earl named among the dead at Agincourt.

entities.name: Marle
entities.body: A French earl named among the dead at Agincourt.

entities.name: Charolois
entities.body: A French lord called to the field.

entities.name: The Governor of Harfleur
entities.body: The governor who yields the town to King Henry.

entities.name: Monsieur Le Fer
entities.body: A French gentleman-soldier taken prisoner by Pistol on the field.

entities.name: The English herald
entities.body: King Henry’s herald, who brings him the count of the dead.

entities.name: The messenger at the French court
entities.body: The messenger who announces the English embassy to the French king.

entities.name: The messenger in the French camp
entities.body: The messenger who brings the French commanders word of the English position.

entities.name: The French ambassador
entities.body: The ambassador who delivers the Dauphin’s answer and his gift to King Henry.

entities.name: The French ambassadors
entities.body: The embassy sent from France to King Henry’s court.

entities.name: The English ambassadors
entities.body: The embassy King Henry sends into France, headed by Exeter.

entities.name: The attendants
entities.body: The attendants waiting on King Henry at his court.

entities.name: The lords
entities.body: The English and French lords at the two courts.

entities.name: The ladies
entities.body: The ladies attending the French queen and princess.

entities.name: The soldiers
entities.body: The soldiers of the English army.

entities.name: The citizens of Harfleur
entities.body: The townspeople on the walls when King Henry demands the town.

entities.name: Sir John Falstaff
entities.body: The old knight of King Henry’s wild years, whose London company Pistol, Bardolph and Nym come from.

snapshots.body: The old knight of King Henry’s wild years; Pistol brings his company word that he has died.

entities.name: King Henry the Fourth
entities.body: King Henry’s father, who took the crown from Richard the Second; the play names him only as the King’s father.

entities.name: King Richard the Second
entities.body: The king King Henry’s father deposed, for whose soul King Henry pays priests to sing.

entities.name: Henry the Sixth
entities.body: King Henry’s infant son, crowned King of France and England after him.

entities.name: King Edward the Third
entities.body: King Henry’s great-grandfather, from whom the claim to France descends.

entities.name: Edward the Black Prince
entities.body: King Henry’s great-uncle, victor over the French at Crécy.
aliases: Edward the Plack Prince of Wales

entities.name: The King of Scots
entities.body: A Scottish king taken prisoner by the English and sent into France.

entities.name: The Emperor
entities.body: The Holy Roman Emperor, expected in England to mediate the peace; he is never named.

entities.name: The Earl of Suffolk
entities.body: An English nobleman who dies at Agincourt beside the Duke of York.

entities.name: Sir Richard Ketly
entities.body: An English knight named among the dead at Agincourt.

entities.name: Davy Gam
entities.body: A Welsh esquire named among the English dead at Agincourt.

entities.name: Talbot
entities.body: An English commander named in King Henry’s roll of remembered names.

entities.name: Doll Tearsheet
entities.body: A London woman of Pistol’s old company, whose death he hears of at the end.

entities.name: Pharamond
entities.body: The legendary Frankish king the French cite as the founder of the Salic law.

entities.name: Charlemagne
entities.body: The Frankish emperor who subdued the Saxons and settled the French beyond the Sala.

entities.name: Charlemain
entities.body: A later Frankish king in Canterbury’s pedigree, father of Lady Lingare; the text keeps him distinct from Charlemagne.

entities.name: King Pepin
entities.body: The Frankish king who deposed Childeric and claimed France through the female line.

entities.name: Childeric
entities.body: The Frankish king deposed by Pepin.

entities.name: Blithild
entities.body: King Clothair’s daughter, from whom Pepin claimed descent.

entities.name: King Clothair
entities.body: A Frankish king, Blithild’s father.

entities.name: Hugh Capet
entities.body: The French king who took the crown from Charles, Duke of Lorraine.

entities.name: Charles, Duke of Lorraine
entities.body: The last male heir of Charlemagne’s line, displaced by Hugh Capet.

entities.name: Lady Lingare
entities.body: Charlemain’s daughter, from whom Hugh Capet traced his title.

entities.name: Lady Ermengare
entities.body: Daughter of Charles, Duke of Lorraine, and ancestress of Queen Isabel the grandmother.

entities.name: Lewis the Emperor
entities.body: A Frankish emperor in Canterbury’s pedigree, son of Charlemagne.

entities.name: King Lewis the Tenth
entities.body: The French king who wore the crown uneasily until his descent through the female line satisfied him.

entities.name: Queen Isabel
entities.body: King Lewis the Tenth’s grandmother in Canterbury’s pedigree; a different Queen Isabel from the French queen in the play.

entities.name: Alexander the Great
entities.body: The Macedonian king, whom Fluellen compares to King Henry.

entities.name: Philip of Macedon
entities.body: Alexander the Great’s father.

entities.name: Cleitus
entities.body: The friend Alexander killed in drink.

entities.name: Pompey the Great
entities.body: The Roman general whose camp Fluellen holds up as a model of discipline.

entities.name: Mark Antony
entities.body: The Roman commander Fluellen names as a byword for valour.

entities.name: Agamemnon
entities.body: The Greek commander at Troy, Fluellen’s measure of greatness of soul.

entities.name: Caesar
entities.body: The Roman conqueror whose triumphal return the Chorus likens King Henry’s to.

entities.name: Brutus
entities.body: The Roman who hid his purpose under an appearance of folly.

entities.name: Herod
entities.body: The king of Judea whose soldiers killed the children, in King Henry’s threat to Harfleur.

entities.name: Adam
entities.body: The first man, whose offending nature the Archbishop says was whipped out of the King.

entities.name: Arthur
entities.body: King Arthur; the Hostess puts Falstaff in “Arthur’s bosom”, meaning Abraham’s.

entities.name: Cadwallader
entities.body: The Welsh king Pistol invokes when he refuses Fluellen’s leek.

entities.name: Saint George
entities.body: The patron saint of England, King Henry’s battle cry.

entities.name: Saint David
entities.body: The patron saint of Wales, whose day the Welsh mark by wearing the leek.

entities.name: Saint Denis
entities.body: The patron saint of France.

entities.name: Saint Crispin and Saint Crispian
entities.body: The paired saints whose feast day falls on the day of the battle.

entities.name: Lucifer
entities.body: The chief of the fallen angels, in Fluellen’s oath.

entities.name: Beelzebub
entities.body: A devil named beside Lucifer in Fluellen’s oath.

entities.name: Barbason
entities.body: A demon whose name Nym says cannot be used to conjure him.

entities.name: Cressid
entities.body: The faithless lover of the Troy story, invoked in Pistol’s insult.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: The Roman king of the gods, who comes in thunder.

entities.name: Mars
entities.body: The Roman god of war.

entities.name: Phoebus
entities.body: The sun god, also called Hyperion here.

entities.name: Hyperion
entities.body: The sun god whose horse the labourer helps to saddle at dawn.

entities.name: Hermes
entities.body: The Greek god whose pipe the Dauphin says his horse outplays.

entities.name: Mercury
entities.body: The winged messenger god; the Chorus calls the English youth “English Mercuries”.

entities.name: Pegasus
entities.body: The winged horse of Greek myth.

entities.name: Perseus
entities.body: The Greek hero who rode Pegasus.

entities.name: Parca
entities.body: The fate who spins and cuts the thread of life.

entities.name: Fortune
entities.body: Fortune painted blind on her rolling stone, turning men’s luck.

entities.name: The gracious empress
entities.body: The reigning queen the Chorus addresses his own London audience about; she is not named in the play.

entities.name: The general from Ireland
entities.body: The commander the Chorus imagines returning from Ireland; the play does not name him.
